nodes.norm_label: what a live upstream actually does

nodes.label: scripts/dev-services.sh Podman Workflow
nodes.rationale: Plain podman through the script is required because the development machine has no podman compose provider; Docker Compose is only an alternative for the full stack.

nodes.label: graphify Knowledge Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Queries should go through graphify query/path/explain before raw grep or file reads to keep context small, and graphify update . keeps the committed graph current because graph.json is rewritten whole on every build.

nodes.label: GraphQL UI Requirement
nodes.rationale: The upstream UI uses GraphQL at /graphql/api/v1 plus graphql-ws /subscriptions for most screens and only the organization list uses REST, so M5 needs a full GraphQL implementation rather than a WebSocket alone.

nodes.label: Terrakube Go
nodes.rationale: A from-scratch Go rewrite of the upstream Java Terrakube platform whose goal is drop-in compatibility, so the existing React UI, Terraform/OpenTofu CLI, provider and API clients keep working unchanged.

nodes.label: Verification Suite (make check / test-race / build)
nodes.rationale: make check runs gofmt, go vet and go test; CI additionally runs go test -race and go build, so concurrency-sensitive changes need make test-race.

nodes.label: Archive Upload Capability UUID
nodes.rationale: Archive uploads are unauthenticated upstream because the unguessable archive UUID acts as the capability; a successful upload deletes the temp_archive row and rollback creates a new history row with serial=1, md5=0, lineage=0.

nodes.label: Compatibility Test Suite
nodes.rationale: internal/tfe/contract_test.go pins the media type, envelopes, discovery and ping headers, and new TFE endpoints must add contract coverage in the same change so the verified contract cannot silently drift.

nodes.label: Terraform Discovery Endpoint
nodes.rationale: GET /.well-known/terraform.json must be mirrored byte-for-byte with login.v1, state.v2, tfe.v2 and tfe.v2.1 so the Terraform CLI discovers the correct login and API surfaces.

nodes.label: Executor Contract
nodes.rationale: The API enqueues a run and the executor claims it, fetches the configuration tarball, injects variables, runs terraform/tofu and reports step/job status; live output goes to Redis while final output and state go to object storage, keeping history.md5/serial/lineage compatible.

nodes.label: GraphQL and Subscription UI Contract
nodes.rationale: The React UI uses GraphQL over HTTP at /graphql/api/v1 for workspace, project and organization screens, graphql-ws subscriptions at /subscriptions for live job updates and SSE with Last-Event-ID for run logs; only the organization list uses REST, so M5 must implement a query/subscription surface or plan a UI rewrite.

nodes.label: Internal Executor JWT
nodes.rationale: Executor calls authenticate with HTTP Basic (username terraform, password an internal JWT) carrying iss/sub/aud TerrakubeInternal and organizationId/workspaceId/jobId/stepId claims signed with the base64url-decoded io.terrakube.token.internal secret; HMAC algorithm follows key length so existing upstream keys stay valid.

nodes.label: Open Compatibility Questions
nodes.rationale: Unresolved areas are the UI GraphQL schema and subscriptions (the biggest hidden cost of reusing the upstream UI), exact JSON:API error objects and RSQL edge cases, Terraform login/OAuth broker behavior, the Kubernetes ephemeral executor contract, and variable encryption/key management.

nodes.label: RSQL Filter Conventions
nodes.rationale: filter[type] uses RSQL (name==prod*, status=in=(failed,cancelled), ; for AND, comma for OR) with sort, page[size]/page[number]/page[totals] and include/fields parameters, matching what the upstream UI and clients send.

nodes.label: State Storage Key Layout
nodes.rationale: Local backend keys use backend/{orgId}/{wsId}/terraform.tfstate and state/... while S3 uses the tfstate/ prefix, mirroring upstream per backend so existing buckets and archives remain readable.

nodes.label: Upstream Environment Variable Aliases
nodes.rationale: Where upstream Terrakube uses an environment variable the Go services accept it as an alias (for example DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL), so existing deployments can reuse their configuration.

nodes.label: Milestone Roadmap (M0-M6)
nodes.rationale: M0 scaffolding, M1 JSON:API management API, M2 /tfstate/v1 state backend, M3 TFE v2 CLI workflow, M4 executor, M5 UI/GraphQL compatibility and M6 RBAC/registry parity; sequencing front-loads what the Terraform CLI needs before the UI and registry surfaces.

nodes.label: Static Bearer Token Auth (TERRAKUBE_AUTH_TOKEN)
nodes.rationale: A single static token is accepted for development and can be left empty to disable the check; PATs and Dex OIDC replace it in M3/M5.

nodes.label: Compatibility Contract
nodes.rationale: Every documented surface was verified against the upstream Java implementation (terrakube-io/terrakube main, 2026-11-14); the project is a rewrite, not a redesign, and upstream behavior wins when in doubt.

nodes.label: Read-Only Review Permission Set
nodes.rationale: Deny-by-default permission list that allows only read, grep, glob and a fixed set of read-only git commands so the reviewer can inspect a diff but never modify the repository.

nodes.label: Migration Safety Checklist
nodes.rationale: Review checklist covering append-only ordering, upstream table/column parity, destructive changes, long locks, missing backfills, indexes/foreign keys/nullability and midway-failure recovery expectations.

nodes.label: services-wipe Is Destructive
nodes.rationale: make services-wipe deletes the local Postgres database, Redis data and MinIO data, so it must never run without an explicit user request.

nodes.label: Compatibility Review Checklist
nodes.rationale: Checklist exists because drop-in compatibility is the product requirement: JSON:API media type and errors array, bodyless DELETE, upstream status codes, filter/sort/paging, relationship links, auth modes and upstream table/column names all have to be verified before a change is accepted.

nodes.label: Append-Only Migrations
nodes.rationale: Applied migration files are immutable and new numbered files are added instead, because existing databases (and imported upstream data) must keep migrating forward deterministically.

nodes.label: Keep Apache-2.0 Attribution
nodes.rationale: The API and schema are derived from Apache-2.0 upstream Terrakube, so LICENSE and the compatibility notes must be preserved when distributing.

nodes.label: Generated sqlc Code Is Off Limits
nodes.norm_label: generated sqlc code is off limits
nodes.rationale: internal/store/*.sql.go is produced by sqlc, so changes belong in internal/store/queries/*.sql followed by make generate; hand edits would be silently overwritten on the next regeneration.

nodes.label: In-Memory Filtering, Sorting and Paging
nodes.rationale: M1 filtering, sorting and paging run over the full collection in memory, which is acceptable for smoke tests but must move into SQL before production.

nodes.label: JSON:API 1.0 Rule
nodes.rationale: Responses must use application/vnd.api+json, failures must return the errors array, and DELETE must send no body or content type so the Elide-generated upstream contract is preserved.

nodes.label: No State LOCK/UNLOCK Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Upstream /tfstate/v1 has no LOCK/UNLOCK methods and the executor configures a plain HTTP backend, so workspace locking is the TFE action POST /workspaces/{id}/actions/lock; inventing a state-lock endpoint would break compatibility.

nodes.label: Secrets Stay Out of Logs and Commits
nodes.norm_label: secrets stay out of logs and commits
nodes.rationale: TERRAKUBE_AUTH_TOKEN is only a development convenience and variable values are still plaintext, so they must never appear in logs, error messages or commits until PATs/Dex and encryption land.

nodes.label: state.v2 vs /tfstate/v1 Gotcha
nodes.rationale: Discovery advertises state.v2 at /remote/state/v2/ but the upstream handler is mounted at /tfstate/v1 and the executor writes an HTTP backend address pointing there, so the advertised path is not the path the CLI uses; both must be verified with the real CLI before changing either.

nodes.label: Upstream Is the Specification
nodes.rationale: The upstream Java implementation defines the contract; endpoints, payloads, status codes, headers, tables and columns must be checked against docs/compat.md and upstream source rather than 'improved', because clients depend on the exact shape.

nodes.label: Variable Values Stored Plaintext
nodes.rationale: Encryption (upstream io.terrakube.encryption.*) is required before the API is exposed beyond local development, so values must not be logged or surfaced in errors in the meantime.

nodes.label: Compatibility-First Contribution Policy
nodes.rationale: Upstream behavior wins for a drop-in-compatible rewrite, so contributors must read docs/compat.md before changing any endpoint, payload, status code or table/column and must update the document when the observed contract changes.

nodes.label: Generated Code and Migration Policy
nodes.rationale: sqlc output under internal/store must be regenerated rather than hand-edited, and migrations are append-only numbered files so applied history is never rewritten.

nodes.label: Upstream Table and Column Parity
nodes.rationale: Migrations intentionally reuse upstream table and column names (varchar(36) UUID keys, created_date/created_by/updated_date/updated_by audit columns) so existing data can be imported and the UI's assumptions hold; extra upstream tables arrive in later migrations.

nodes.label: JSON:API 1.0 Conventions
nodes.rationale: The upstream API is Elide-generated JSON:API 1.0, so the media type application/vnd.api+json, the errors array and a bodyless DELETE are non-negotiable for client compatibility.

nodes.label: No LOCK/UNLOCK on /tfstate/v1
nodes.rationale: The executor writes an HTTP backend with only an address, so Terraform performs no state locking; workspace locking is the TFE action POST /workspaces/{id}/actions/lock, and a locked workspace still accepts run creation because the lock blocks dispatch rather than the API call.

nodes.label: Discovery state.v2 vs /tfstate/v1 Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Upstream advertises state.v2 at /remote/state/v2/ but mounts the handler at /tfstate/v1 and the executor's backend override points at /tfstate/v1/.../backend/terraform.tfstate, so the discovery document is mirrored byte-for-byte while state is served at /tfstate/v1.

nodes.label: Variable Encryption Gap
nodes.rationale: Upstream encrypts variable values with io.terrakube.encryption.*, while the Go implementation stores them plaintext; encryption and key management must land before variable values are exposed.

nodes.label: Drop-in Compatibility Goal
nodes.rationale: The backend is replaced while the existing React UI, Terraform/OpenTofu CLI (cloud block and remote backend), provider and API clients keep working, which is why API paths, payload shapes and table names are taken from upstream.
